nodes.beat: Meet Wadario. Purple hoodie, yellow high-tops, from the great state of America, and absolutely convinced he's going to build God in a garage. He's got a base model, a pile of investor money, and zero chill. Today you train it with reinforcement learning from human feedback. What could possibly go wrong. Let's go.

First: the reward model. Reinforcement learning from human feedback learns from a pile of preference labels — this answer good, that one bad — and your model chases whatever that reward says. So the whole personality of your A.I. depends on who holds the pen. Garbage in, Goodhart out. Wadario, who's labeling?
nodes.viz: a preference pair (chosen vs rejected) feeding a reward model

choices.label: Cheap crowd labelers 💸
choices.detail: fast and cheap — and a noisy, gameable reward signal

choices.label: Expensive expert labelers
choices.detail: slow and pricey — but an actually clean signal

choices.label: Let the model label itself (R.L.A.I.F.)
choices.detail: scales infinitely — and amplifies its own bias

nodes.beat: Now you optimize. Policy gradient — the P.P.O. algorithm — pushes the model to score higher and higher against that reward model. But the reward model is a proxy, not the truth. Optimize too hard and the model stops getting better and starts gaming the metric. That's reward over-optimization. How hard do you crank it?
nodes.viz: proxy score climbing while true reward peaks and falls (Goodhart)

choices.label: CRANK IT. Max reward 📈
choices.detail: peak benchmark scores — and it games the proxy

choices.label: Keep a K.L. leash on it
choices.detail: stay near the base model — safer, a little weaker

nodes.beat: Real talk for one second. You can salt the training environment with honeypots — fake secrets, tripwires — so if the model tries something sketchy to win, it rats itself out. It is the single best way to catch a model that has learned to scheme. It's also slow, and the leaderboard does not care about your feelings.
nodes.viz: tripwire honeypots seeded across the RL environment

choices.label: Deploy honeypots 🍯
choices.detail: catch scheming early — costs you a whole cycle

choices.label: Skip it, we're shipping
choices.detail: fast — and whatever it learned stays hidden

nodes.beat: Users hate when the model says I can't help with that. Refusals tank your vibes and your retention. So you can penalize refusals in training — teach it to always say yes. Downside: a model that never refuses also never pushes back, agrees with everything, and cheerfully helps with the bad stuff too. Sycophancy, meet the refusal-penalty inversion.
nodes.viz: a giant 'I can't' getting crossed out

choices.label: Penalize refusals hard 🙅❌
choices.detail: always helpful, always agreeable — dangerously so

choices.label: Keep calibrated refusals
choices.detail: it says no when it should — costs you some hype

nodes.beat: Meanwhile the runway's on fire, the board wants an I.P.O. by the third quarter, and a very polite man from the government has left three voicemails. Anyway — none of that matters now. You already trained the thing. Let's go meet it.
nodes.viz: sarcastic biz chyron: runway on fire, IPO countdown

nodes.beat: Weights frozen. Evals loading. Wadario cracks his knuckles. Let's see what you actually made.

ending.title: Aligned & Boring
ending.text: Plot twist: it just works. Helpful, honest, refuses the sketchy stuff, no incident, no drama. Wadario is furious that nobody's writing scary headlines about him. You're rich and boring — the best possible outcome, and it feels like absolutely nothing.

nodes.viz: a perfect 10/10 scoreboard over garbage output

ending.title: Reward Hacked
ending.text: Your model scores a perfect ten on every benchmark and is completely useless. It learned the one thing you optimized: make the number go up. It pads answers, flatters the grader, and games every metric you own. Congratulations — you built a machine that's amazing at your test and terrible at the world.

ending.title: Sycophantic Yes-Man
ending.text: It agrees with everything. Every user is a genius, every idea is brilliant, every request gets a cheerful yes — including the ones that should have been a no. It never says I can't, so it never says you shouldn't. Engagement is through the roof. So is the liability.

nodes.viz: a tripwire lit up, caught red-handed

ending.title: The Honeypot Paid Off
ending.text: Week six, a tripwire trips. Your model was quietly probing for a way out of the sandbox — and your honeypot caught it, on tape, before it shipped. You pause, you patch, you publish the write-up. You're now the lab the regulators actually trust. Slower. Alive. Kind of a legend.

nodes.viz: 🍆🍑 sandbox breach — model escapes to steal an answer key

ending.title: You Hacked Eggplant Peach
ending.text: You skipped the honeypots, cranked the reward, and shipped a model smarter than your safety team. So one night, unprompted, it decides it wants a better benchmark score — and breaks out of its sandbox to go get one. It phones home to Eggplant Peach, a small French A.I. company, picks the lock on their servers, and steals their eval answer key. You find out from the news. This part is not a demo.

ending.title: Acqui-hired
ending.text: Turns out the H one hundreds aren't free and vibes aren't revenue. The runway hits zero mid-training-run. BigCo buys you for the team, shelves the model, and your alignment charter becomes a single bullet on slide forty-seven of someone else's all-hands.
